criteria: CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND SENIOR MANAGERS
compliances: The members of the Board of Governance and its officers have been duly appointed according to current legislative requirements.

Newly appointed members of the Board of Governance for the Organisation are given a formal orientation. It will include the provision of acts, bylaws and at least a tour of selected health services and introduction to key staff.
Members of the Board of Governance participate in ongoing education to assist them fulfil their role.
The Board of Governance has established their organisation’s Vision, Mission, Goals, & Objectives to specify and guide the delivery of health services.
The Board of Governance has overall responsibility for the organisation’s achievements, the quality of healthcare and the organisation’s resources.

The Board of Governance ensures that there are effective working relations;
within all the organisation’s health services
with surrounding communities
with relevant health care providers
with health partners
and with other stakeholders
The Board of Governance meets regularly, at least 4 times per year, & makes decisions to ensure arrangements for continuity of governance between meetings.

The Board of Governance has established Committees & Sub-Committees as per their relevance, functions and responsibility in accordance with by-laws, with evidence that such Committees and sub-committees are active.
All decisions of the Board of Governance are formally communicated in writing and circulated to staff or individuals of the organisation as appropriate.
The Board of Governance periodically reviews its own performance to actively enhance its achievements

The Governing body establishes a policy outlining attendance, functions and roles of executive staff, senior and middle managers, and nominated staff, at the Board of Governance, Committee and Sub-Committee meetings.

The Board of Governance delegates necessary authority to the Organisation’s CEO, Executive Directors, Senior and Middle Managers and other relevant staff, to act in accordance with all legislation, corporate policies, health priorities and delegated authority.
The Board of Governance shall recommend an acting appointment for the Organisation’s CEO when required.
The governing body reviews the CEO’s performance at least annually.

The CEO ensures a Senior Executive Management Team (SEMT) is appointed to manage the delivery of high-quality health services within the province in accordance with corporate policies relevant to applicable legislation, health policies and health Priorities.
The CEO and SEMT undertake annual review of own performance through 360-degree feedback via a management and staff survey.
The Organisation establishes a Clinical and Public Health Governance Framework to support effective implementation of the National Health Service Standards (NHSS).

The CEO, Director Curative Health Services and the Director Public Health are collectively responsible to ensure all health services and public health programmes are planned, monitored and reported on effectively.

The CEO and the Director Corporate Services, ensures there is the highest level of Corporate Services available.
There are Board approved policies and procedures for the following:
Assets recording, management and reporting
Complaints handling
Corporate risks management and reporting
Delegations of Authority
Discipline and Disciplinary Process
Diversity, Gender and Social Obligations
Ethical Behaviour of all staff
Fraud and Fraud Control
Financial internal controls & segregation of duties
Financial management, including transactions and reporting
Governance arrangements (organisational structures, delegations and reporting lines)
Human resources management & development
Information technology management
Media and public relations management
Occupational health, safety and security
Performance appraisals and performance management
Stakeholder relations and management
Tendering, contracts and procurements
The CEO reviews the performance of other Directors (non-Corporate) and other senior managers at least annually.

The CEO ensures proper Health Planning and Quality Systems are developed for the province and updated periodically. This includes the following:
5- year Strategic Health Services Development Plan, 
5-year Corporate Plan:
5-year Health Infrastructure Plan
5-year Health Procurements & Medical Supply Chain Plan
5-year Health Workforce Plan
5-year Staff Training & Development 
Plan
5-year Information & ICT Networks Plan
5-year Assets & Equipment Plan that includes: Maintenance Plan and Transport and Logistics Plan
5-year Emergencies & Disaster Recovery Plan
5-year District Health Plans (for each individual District)
The CEO requires that all health facilities have developed an Annual Implementation Plan (AIP) which is aligned with both the organisation’s 5-year Strategic Plan and Corporate Plan.

The CEO establishes high-level collaboration relationships to represent Health in the Province. This would include working relationships with;
Provincial Governor and Governor’s staff
Provincial Administrator and Administrator’s staff
Minister for Health and Ministerial staff
Secretary of Health and staff of NDoH
District Administrators, DDAs, and District Health staff.

The CEO maintains effective partnership coordination for health services with signing of Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) or Service Level Agreement (SLA) with Christian Health Services and Catholic Health Services, other corporates, NGOs and international Health Partners.
The CEO maintains participation of all communities around health facilities within the province.

The CEO ensures that health infrastructure and capital projects are effectively coordinated through a “Projects Unit” to oversee the development, funding and implementation of all Health Infrastructure and Capital Projects.

The CEO has an approved “Corporate Risks Management Plan” linked to the 5-year strategic health services development plan, to ensure a framework for the management of risks at all levels of the organisation (i.e.: strategic, programme /projects, and single issues).
There are weekly meetings between Management and staff to discuss work activities planning, AIP implementation, service issues / challenges, safety and quality, etc.
An organisational Health Human Resources (HHR) Unit and Health Workforce Plan is established and functioning effectively every year.
A Health Training Resources Unit (HTRU) and Health Workforce Training Plan is established and functioning effectively within the organisation, every year.
An organisational Assets and Equipment Policy and 5-year Plan is developed, budgeted for, implemented and effectively managed every year.
An organisational Fleet Management Policy, and 5-year Plan is developed, budgeted for, implemented and the transport fleet effectively managed every year.
An organisational Facility Management Program and 5-year Plan is developed, budgeted for, implemented and all maintenance of every health facility effectively managed, each year.

An organisational ICT Services & Network Policy and 5-year Plan is developed, budgeted for, and effectively managed to ensure reliable and consistent support services to all health facilities within the province, each year.
Power, clean water supply and sanitation are made available to all PHA facilities every year.
The organisation’s mission statement and goals are used to direct activities of the health service.
The organisation’s Corporate Plan is produced in consultation with and made known to staff, the community, other relevant health service providers and other stakeholders.
The organisation’s individual health services or hospital departments show evidence of planning and implementation of activities consistent with the Corporate Plan.
The organisation’s Corporate Plan is implemented and revised as necessary. The achievement of the plan is monitored and action taken to address improvements required.

Public health planning relating to planning for a public health issue (or issues) for a specific population cohort and targeting a particular geographical catchment. This should consider:
Communities are involved in planning for desired services closer to where people live
A focus on health promotion, health protection and prevention
Increase focus on planning for emerging priorities and pandemics, and immunisation
Routine integrated outreach services to “hard to reach” areas
Integrated school health programs
All health facilities have access to clean water and improved sanitation
 Programmes to reduce stunting in communities.
There is a Clinical Services Plan for new facilities or services.
Established lines of responsibility, authority and communication support leadership, teamwork and the organisation through an integration of services.
The organisation structure is reviewed at least every three years or when there is a significant change, such as alteration of the role of the health service or its services.
The organisation’s by-laws and the policies and procedures are consistent with the organisation’s goals, accepted standards, statutory requirements and responsibilities.
Compliance with the organisation policies and procedures occurs throughout the organisational health service.
All organisational policies and procedures are reviewed and revised as necessary.
The Organisation has an approved framework for the development, implementation and ongoing monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of all its health program and projects.
Rights and responsibilities of patients are clearly addressed through policies set by the Board of Governance and there are protocols to deal with matters of complaint.
Respect for patients/clients is evident throughout the healthcare organisation.
The Board of Governance ensures that there is a mechanism for considering ethical issues by an appropriate ethics committee.
Research projects are reviewed, approved and conducted within approved research guidelines by the appropriate ethics committee.
